paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, end of chapter 3, speaking in Shmuel’s name and disagreeing with Rabbi Hoshaya. In Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 8, Rabbi Tanchuma speaks in his name; in Pesachim, beginning of chapter 4, Chinena the father of R' Yinta speaks in his name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:1 has Chinena, father of Rav Yinta, reporting Rabbi Benayah. Hyman’s supplied full רבי ינטה is retained as Rabbi Yinta; the named witness has Rav.

The checked Sanhedrin passage has Rav Bannay reporting Shmuel beside Rabbi Hoshaya; Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Benayah, and the Pesachim passage has Chinena, father of Rav Yinta, reporting Rabbi Benayah. These forms are compared without identifying every occurrence as one person. Hyman’s abbreviated heading is retained as R' Benai. The supplied notice also abbreviates Yinta’s title; the older note’s description of full רבי does not match that supplied wording, while the named Pesachim witness explicitly has Rav. Its statement that “Rabbi Yinta” is retained describes the earlier English; the present translation keeps the supplied abbreviation as R' Yinta.
